transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-09-02 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Ethan Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Rodriguez (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SA), Nina Park (Redwood CSM); Olivia Zhang (Aurora Head of ML), Marcus Hale (Platform), Priya Anand (CTO), Diego Ruiz (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto): Discussed workload telemetry and traffic modeling for an initial POC; agreed on data to collect (7 days traces), three-phase benchmark plan, and deliverables. Next meeting: benchmark run scheduling.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Ethan: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. uh quick roll call — can you hear me?
[00:10] Olivia: yes loud and clear, thanks Ethan.
[00:15] Ethan: awesome. the goal today is to nail down the workload shape and success criteria for the POC so we can size capacity and design the benchmark. we'll walk through your traffic, maya will talk bench harness and scaling knobs, and then we capture next steps.
[00:30] Maya: hi team, i pulled some examples of the kinds of tests we run: steady-state qps, burst tests, concurrency sweep, and token distribution-driven runs. i wanna understand your real qps curves.
[00:45] Olivia: great — quick context: Aurora Retail runs a mix of user-facing product search completions and assistant flows for merchandisers. typical mix is about 60% short prompts (search autocomp), 40% session prompts (chat-like).
[01:10] Marcus: to add — our peak shopping hours are 14:00-17:00 UTC, we see bursts tied to promotions; last flash sale spiked to ~1.2k qps for ~90 seconds before we rate-limited.
[01:35] Ethan: good. that burst number is helpful. can you give typical sustained qps?
[01:40] Olivia: sustained is usually 180-220 qps across the whole fleet, global. concurrency per instance varies because we have edge services but at the model layer we observed about 45 concurrent requests typically.
[02:05] Maya: what are your p95/p99 latency targets from the app perspective?
[02:10] Priya: business target is p95 < 350ms for short flows; for session completions we're ok up to 800ms p95 as long as p99 stays reasonable.
[02:25] Maya: ok that gives us SLO bands. for the POC we should aim to prove p95 under 350ms for the short prompt mix at 200 qps sustained and show graceful degradation during a 1k qps 120s burst.
[02:45] Diego: on data — we can provide telemetry, timestamps, token counts, and a sample of input payloads. we will need guidance on redaction.
[02:58] Ethan: perfect, we'll share a template for traces. please try to include a week (7 days) with at least one promotion day.
[03:10] Olivia: noted.
[03:15] Maya: can you share typical input/output token stats now? means, tails, anything?
[03:22] Olivia: approximate: short search prompts mean input tokens ~18, output ~6; session prompts mean input ~120, output ~50. overall weighted mean input ~64, output ~28. 95th percentile for input is around 340 tokens when customers paste order history.
[03:50] Samir: that 95th input tail matters a lot for KV cache and decoding time. are you also doing streaming token-by-token to the client?
[03:58] Marcus: yes for search we stream partial suggestions; for session completions we stream only final chunks sometimes.
[04:10] Maya: ok — streaming changes latency behaviour; we'll include streaming vs non-streaming scenarios.
[04:20] Ethan: let's talk concurrency and model choices. are you bound to a specific model family or open to quantized variants?
[04:30] Priya: prefer staying on open LLMs due to licensing, but we're open to quantized and trimmed models if quality is preserved. cost is a factor.
[04:45] Maya: good. for the POC we propose three candidate configs: 1) baseline hosted medium-sized open model (e.g., 13B), 2) quantized 70B on dedicated infra (8-bit/4-bit tuned), and 3) Redwood-optimized runtime with prefix caching enabled. we'll measure throughput/cost/latency for each.
[05:10] Olivia: sound plan. what about batching? we actually care about tail latency for UI flows so large batching hurts us.
[05:20] Maya: yes we'll test continuous batching with small batch windows (2-8ms) and also per-request routing. we'll surface the batching tradeoffs in the results sheet.
[05:35] Ethan: any regulatory constraints, EU data residency or encryption needs?
[05:40] Priya: EU customers are big; data residency may matter for certain accounts. but for this POC traces are anonymized and can be shared to Redwood's secure bucket. we need SOC2 artifact review later.
[05:58] Ethan: noted — we'll attach our SOC2 summary and redaction guidelines.
[06:10] Marcus: one more thing — what load generator are you recommending? we prefer something we can run from our infra to avoid egress.
[06:20] Maya: we'll produce k6 scripts and a lightweight client harness in Node/Python that replays token timelines and simulates streaming. we can share both options.
[06:35] Olivia: perfect. can you walk through the benchmark phases?
[06:40] Maya: yeah — three phases: Phase A baseline functional (small scale correctness and QoS checks), Phase B steady-state throughput (sustained 200-250 qps for 30 minutes), Phase C stress and burst (simulate 1k qps bursts of 60-180s and concurrency sweeps). we'll collect latency percentiles, cpu/gpu utilization, memory, cost estimate per 1M tokens, and quality checks (perplexity/heuristic pass on canned prompts).
[07:20] Diego: about quality checks — we can provide golden prompts and expected outputs for several flows.
[07:28] Maya: excellent — that will let us run auto-evals.
[07:35] Olivia: timeline wise, how long between us sending traces and you running benchmarks?
[07:40] Ethan: once we get traces and confirm redaction it takes ~5 business days to prepare the harness and infra. then we need a 2-3 day window to run experiments and an extra day to produce the report. so roughly 2 weeks end-to-end if nothing blocks.
[08:00] Priya: that's reasonable. we want success criteria spelled out.
[08:05] Ethan: agreed. proposed success criteria: 1) For short-prompt mix (60% short): p95 <= 350ms at sustained 200 qps; 2) For session flows: p95 <= 800ms at expected concurrency; 3) During a 1k qps 120s burst the system degrades gracefully (no hard failures, errors <0.5%); 4) Cost per 1M tokens less than customer's internal target (we requested the target via CRM) — if not, show path to optimize via quantization/caching.
[08:50] Olivia: we'll confirm the internal cost target and share with you.
[08:58] Maya: about observability — we'll require token-level metrics, per-request breakdown, and a mapping between requests and traces. can you attach request IDs in the trace?
[09:10] Diego: yes we can include request_id, timestamp, and input/output token counts.
[09:20] Maya: perfect.
[09:22] Ethan: let's talk about routing and fallback. if peak capacity is hit what's your preference for fallback? degrade to smaller model, or rate-limit?
[09:32] Priya: degrade to smaller model for core UX and rate-limit for non-critical background tasks.
[09:40] Samir: technical note — we'll prototype automatic fallbacks in the POC by routing to a quantized variant. we can measure quality delta.
[09:55] Marcus: what about multi-region routing? our traffic is global.
[10:00] Maya: we can run distributed bench agents and measure cross-region latency; for POC we'll focus on primary region and one secondary.
[10:10] Olivia: can you outline the deliverables from Redwood after the run?
[10:15] Ethan: deliverables: benchmark report (latency percentiles, throughput, util, cost estimate), recommendations (batching, quantization profile), and an ops playbook for scaling and fallbacks.
[10:28] Priya: include a recommended Dedicated config and pricing ballpark.
[10:32] Ethan: yes — a committed config + cost delta vs hosted.
[10:35] Maya: i want to capture a quick example workload profile now for the spreadsheet: 70% of requests are <= 80 tokens input, but 5% are >300 tokens; weighted mean input 64, output 28; average tokens per inference ~92. does that sound right?
[10:58] Olivia: yes that's our current observed distribution.
[11:05] Maya: ok i'll build the traffic model with those percentiles; we'll simulate a day and a flash sale day with injected bursts.
[11:18] Diego: on infra access — we can run the hammer from our VPC and point to Redwood endpoints if you provide temporary creds. is there a secure upload for the traces?
[11:28] Ethan: yes we'll provide an S3 presigned or a secure Share link; we'll document the redaction steps in the template.
[11:35] Priya: one small ask: can you include an estimate of GPU-hours for the POC run? we need that for cost signoff.
[11:42] Samir: we will include GPU-hour estimates for each model config and per-phase; early estimate: Phase B steady-state at 200 qps for 30 min on 70B quantized might use ~6-8 GPU-hours depending on batching and instance shape — we'll refine after we see traces.
[12:05] Olivia: thanks.
[12:10] Ethan: i want to call out some risks: heavy 95th token tails could blow up tail latency and cost; streaming adds complexity; and we need to be careful with streaming + quantization combination — might cause jitter.
[12:30] Priya: understood — we'll share the highest tail scenarios and identify flows to exclude from streaming if needed.
[12:40] Maya: one more technical: for accurate p99 we'll enable high-res tracing and token-level timestamps on the runtime; small overhead but needed for diagnosis.
[12:55] Diego: that's fine.
[13:00] Ethan: time to recap and confirm next steps.
[13:05] Ethan: recap: Aurora will produce 7 days of traces and golden prompts; Redwood will deliver a benchmark harness, S3 upload instructions, and proposed benchmark schedule. we aim to run the benchmark week of 9/15.
[13:25] Olivia: sounds good.
[13:30] Maya: action items captured — we'll send the spreadsheet and harness links.
[13:35] Priya: thanks everyone.
[13:40] Ethan: thanks, we'll follow up in email with attachments.
[13:45] Meeting ends.
